purpose: The colour every declared guard is expected to be, and — for the ones expected to be red — who owns that red, why it is there, and what would close it. Read ci/check_open_reds.py for the argument; the short form is that an accepted red and a new red must not look the same, and before this file the only record of an acceptance was a number somebody remembered.
how_to_add_an_entry: An entry with expect=red is a LEASE, not a grant. It needs an owner who can actually close it, a `closes_when` that names the observable event, a `signature` that is the exact red being accepted (not a wildcard), and a `review_by` after which the lane fails until somebody re-reads it. If you cannot write `closes_when`, you do not have an accepted red, you have an unowned one, and the honest thing is to leave the lane failing.
how_to_remove_an_entry: Delete it. The screen will tell you when: an expect=red entry whose check has gone green is FAIL(condition=stale_acceptance). You do not have to remember to come back; the mechanism asks.

not_declared_here.tests/union_check.py --run: Its five reds are declared here INDIVIDUALLY (harness_census_drift, kv_caller_bind_reading, proof_ledger_writer_refuses x2, and the device-only matmulnbits one below) rather than as one entry, because `FAIL(condition=union_red)` is a returncode, and that returncode sums 3 FAIL(condition) with 2 ERROR(instrument). That is the same incommensurable-sum defect as the '48 failures' headline I carried for three sessions — 42 ledger + 4 instrument + 2 residual, three different kinds of thing behind one number. An entry for the sum would accept all five as one red and go on accepting a sixth. Tiers 1-2 of union_check are PRECONDITIONS and never render a colour at all, so there is nothing there for this screen to rule on.
not_declared_here.tests/ops/test_matmulnbits.py::test_laye: Its colour depends on a device: it is red on a lane with a GPU (the run falls back to CPUExecutionProvider) and green-by-skip on a host-free runner. This screen runs host-free, so it cannot observe that check's colour, and a colour this screen cannot observe must not be declared here — UNOBSERVABLE is not green, and an entry that is satisfied by a skip is an acceptance granted by an absence. It belongs in a device-lane register when one exists. Named here so that its omission is a statement rather than a gap.
not_declared_here.the 12 Windows-only failures: Collapsed to 1 after Mouse's two-digest schema landed, and the survivor is a device-only fp16 depth drift routed to Mouse/Switch. Same reason as above: not host-free.

checks.reason: The two-polarity suite for everything in ci/, MINUS the three census-extent tests, which are their own entry below. This entry is the whole reason the file exists: for four sessions I reported this suite as '132 passed, 3 failed (the known census reds)' and today, post-merge, it was 4 — the fourth being four `if: env.BUILD_SKIPPED != '1'` guards whose writer my own previous commit had deleted, reintroduced by the merge and caught by my own build-precondition screen. Reading the node ids found it; reading the count would not have. Narrowing here is the amplifier, not a cost saving (Trinity's principle from the contention gate): a whole-suite entry accepted as red absorbs every future red in 135 tests, whereas this one goes red on the next one.
checks.closes_when: n/a — this is expected green and must stay green.

checks.owner: mouse (counters + ops/), switch (vk/ env switches), tank (allocator env switches)
checks.reason: These three are the reds I have been calling 'known' since session 14, and writing them down is the first time anyone has had to say WHOSE they are. All three assert EXIT_PASS from the census-extent screen, and the screen is correctly reporting 12 instrumented surfaces that no census mechanism observes: counters.rs compile_calls / compute_calls / subgraphs_stub (Mouse), and nine env switches — BACKEND_PROBE, DUMP_OUTPUT_BYTES, VERBOSE (Switch), CLAIM_DEBUG, CLAIM_LOG, GEMV_PACKED (Mouse), DEVICE_MEMORY, QUARANTINE_SPANS, VA_RESERVE_MIB (Tank). None of them is mine and none can be closed from ci/. GEMV_PACKED is the interesting one and already has a written verdict: the switch enters the program as specialization constant index 5 and keys the pipeline cache, but no artifact the project produces records a pipeline key or a spec constant, so every kernel observation we hold is silent about which kernel it observed.
checks.closes_when: Each owner either wires a census mechanism to their surface or records it out of frame with a reason. The entry is deleted when the three tests go green; until then the screen reports it every run with these names attached, which is strictly more than the count did.

checks.reason: The general fix for `BUILD_SKIPPED=1; exit 0` — one missing tracked file converting thirty steps to green. It went red on this very merge (BP2, four dormant guards arriving with Trinity's contention-gate steps), which is the second half of the point: the lane that CAUSED the failure (my deletion of the writer) was not the lane that REPORTED it (her steps).

Every gate step in the workflow must map to a declared Check. This screen rules on colour; that one rules on coverage. Kept as two tools over one tree on purpose — see ci/check_open_reds.py's frame note.

Nine `pub fn` accessors arrived on rust/src/counters.rs and rust/src/allocator.rs with the two-digest schema and NOTHING CALLS ANY OF THEM: clear_session_devices, device_unattributed_forms, output_residency, proven_elsewhere_forms, source_cosmetic_forms, specialisation_delta_forms, specialisation_unrecorded_forms, subject_changed_forms, unproven_decline_forms. The JSON emitter reads the statics directly and never goes through the accessors, so the accessors are a public surface with no reader. This red is TRUE and must not be baselined: audit_instruments.py's own comment says baselining an open item 'would turn an open item into a green tick, which is the one thing a census must never do'. The frame arm of the same check (two undeclared bench/ modules, spirv_simt.py and test_weight_reread.py) WAS mine and is fixed, so the only remaining red is this one.
checks.closes_when: Mouse gives each of the nine accessors a caller, or removes it, and then runs `python rust/tools/audit_instruments.py --write-baseline`. At that moment this entry becomes FAIL(condition=stale_acceptance) and must be deleted.

checks.reason: A test whose subject is a TRACKED ARTIFACT, `bench/results/kv_device_residency-callerbind.json`. The test asserts the reading contains 'CUDA' — i.e. that `device_type='gpu'` is routed to CUDA regardless of vendor and a plugin EP is therefore unaddressable by the documented spelling. The artifact was re-taken at 872d739 and now records `by_device_type_and_vendor: 'OK'`. So either the obstacle went away and the assertion is stale, or the re-take was made under conditions that do not answer the same question. Exactly one of the two readings is right and I cannot tell which from the artifact alone — which is why this is an owned red and not a fix.
checks.closes_when: Switch re-takes the caller-bind reading and either updates the assertion (the obstacle is gone) or restores the reading (the re-take answered a different question). Either way the entry is deleted and the screen reports stale_acceptance until it is.

checks.reason: Both tests now raise `SystemExit: REFUSING to write an entry ... the run reported source_digest=''` on BOTH platforms. This is a defect INTRODUCED BY the two-digest repair, not one it failed to fix: the writer's new subject-witness precondition fires inside tests that were written to exercise the refusal path with a synthetic run. They are ERROR(instrument) in the R13 lane summary, not FAIL(condition) — a lane with an instrument error is not a lane that ran — and this register keeps that distinction rather than counting them as two more reds.
checks.closes_when: Mouse either gives the synthetic runs a source_digest or teaches the writer to distinguish a run with no witness from a run whose witness is deliberately absent. Filed alongside RAI-012.
